new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (198 pp., A5, author metadata "Giulio Soravia", AMS Acta 2367) re-read with extracted text. PDF p. 16 = printed p. 4, sect. 1.1 Phonology, immediately after the phoneme inventory and the note that the spelling follows Indonesian ejaan baru, reads verbatim: "A further remark may be made for the existence of long vowels, though with no distinctive value and mostly in monosyllables, which are left unmarked in our spelling. No significative stress is audible either." It is followed directly by "The following minimal pairs justify the above inventory:" and the minimal-pair list; there is no separate suprasegmental section. a full-text search for stress/accent the full text layer for stress/…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The author reports hearing no significant (perceptible/phonologically relevant) word stress in Alas; vowel length is likewise non-distinctive. No stress position is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only other prosodic remark in the book is that yes/no questions are 'marked by a particular intonation' (sect. 3.5, p. ~ Clauses).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, impressionistic auditory judgement from 1983/1985 fieldwork in Kutacane; no instrumental data. The remark is one sentence inside the phoneme-inventory discussion; there is no separate suprasegmentals section.
new_statements.identity_note: Soravia describes the Alas dialect as spoken in and around Kutacane, Kabupaten Aceh Tenggara (main informant Drs. Sjech Ahmaddin; fieldwork 1983, 1985). Glottolog's bata1292 'Batak Alas-Kluet' also covers Kluet (Aceh Selatan), which Soravia does not treat; the Kluet-specific reports (Akbar 1982, Ismail 1984, Ismail et al. 1990) were not readable. No separate Glottolog dialect code for Kluet was seen in the records consulted.

new_statements.quote: 2.4 Prosodi. Tekanan kata, nada, dan panjang-pendek bunyi dalam bahasa Alas tidak bersifat fonemis; artinya, tidak menimbulkan perubahan makna. Yang terjadi, dipanjangkannya bunyi vokal akhir beberapa kata dasar tertentu karena terjadi penyatuan dengan bunyi e dari akhiran -en (Penelitian "Struktur Bahasa Alas", 1977/1978:18-19). Contoh: minggu 'minggu' -> minggu:an 'mingguan'; tapi 'tepi' -> tapi:an 'tepian'.
new_statements.translation: 2.4 Prosody. Word stress, pitch (tone), and length of sounds in the Alas language are not phonemic; that is, they do not bring about a change of meaning. What does occur is lengthening of the final vowel of certain base words through fusion with the sound e of the suffix -en (research report 'Struktur Bahasa Alas', 1977/1978:18-19). Examples: minggu 'week' -> minggu:an 'weekly'; tapi 'edge' -> tapi:an 'edge, bank'.

new_statements.relation_note: Same type of statement as the existing Soravia 2007 record ('No significative stress is audible either'): stress in Alas is not distinctive. Adds that pitch and length are likewise non-phonemic and points to Struktur Bahasa Alas 1977/1978:18-19 (not located online) as the primary phonological description. No placement is given by either source, so nothing conflicts.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (like pitch and length) is declared non-phonemic / non-distinctive in Alas; the book gives no statement of where stress falls. The only prosodic phenomenon described is phonetic lengthening of a stem-final vowel when it fuses with the e of suffix -en. The section explicitly says the phonology is not described in detail because the data are written orthographically, and it defers to Struktur Bahasa Alas (1977/1978) pp. 18-19. Read here as 'no contrastive word stress per source' (same type as Soravia's 'no significative stress'), not as a positive claim that stress is phonetically absent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only remark beyond the non-phonemic statement is the -en fusion lengthening (minggu:an, tapi:an)
new_statements.identity_note: Akbar et al. 1984 describe Alas, dialek Babussalam, Kabupaten Aceh Tenggara (5 informants over 35; Bab I 1.5, printed p. 2), i.e. the same Kutacane-area Alas as Soravia 2007. Ismail et al. 1990 describe bahasa Kluet of Kecamatan Kluet Utara (Kota Fajar), Kabupaten Aceh Selatan -- the Kluet member of Glottolog bata1292 Batak Alas-Kluet, a different variety from the catalog's 'Alas' record.
